type: traversal order of the loader (graph reachability, not sequential)
structure: How the engine finds the objects it constructs: pointer traversal from the section-1 header roots

location.offset: section 1 + 0x1C (first object), + 0x20.. (table), block before the first object

meaning: The loader does not walk section 1 sequentially: 272 objects scattered between 0x186888 and 0x450C18 (CameraInfo 15, tfbActorInfo 15, ScriptSet 9, ValueInfo 11, Op*/Measurement/Slider script types ...) keep their raw file bytes in RAM while their neighbours are rewritten; 179 of them have no incoming pointer word at all. Every object with an incoming pointer from a rewritten object is itself rewritten. An object appended to section 1 without an incoming pointer is therefore never fixed up, never constructed and never becomes a gameplay entity: this is the structural cause of the first M3 failure (clone appended and written into a word inside an object, not into any list). Making a clone alive requires a pointer from a visited structure: for the spawn owner that structure is the section-1 header table (entry #1074), so the reachable clone adds a table entry and rebases all 160 575 shifted pointer words.

evidence.probe: ssa-archive experiment ptr-scan --dimensions (ptr-scan2.json, ptr-scan2-section1.bin) + igz fixups
evidence.summary: 272 unvisited objects scattered among 21 408 visited ones (18 373 visited objects lie inside the unvisited range); 179/272 have no confirmed pointer to them

evidence.probe: static reachability over the confirmed pointer words (scratch reach-vs-live.mjs)
evidence.summary: traversal from table+block roots over the 157 690 confirmed pointer words reaches 19 848 objects; 191 objects are both unreachable and unvisited; remaining differences come from the first-object root and inline lists

CONTRADICTION of the root hypothesis: with table entry #1074 redirected from the spawn owner to an appended clone (no relocation), the original owner and its physics model were fully constructed (class pointers, position copied) while the clone stayed raw and the load froze. Table entries do not drive construction; whatever enumerates objects reached the owner without any file pointer to its header other than its child back-pointer.
